literal: Even if blossomed in clusters, scentless flowers they are like: what was learned, to understand, having expanded, those who do not speak.
translation: Those who cannot clearly explain what they have learned so that others understand are like flowers that blossom in clusters but yield no fragrance.
modern: தாம் கற்றவற்றை மற்றவர்கள் உணரும்படி விரிவாக எடுத்துச் சொல்ல முடியாதவர்கள், கொத்தாக மலர்ந்திருந்தாலும் மணம் வீசாத மலர்களைப் போன்றவர்கள்.
explanation: This couplet compares learned people who lack the skill of communication to scentless flowers. The phrase 'இண்ருழ்த்தும் நாறா மலர்' (flowers that bloom in clusters but lack fragrance) creates a vivid image of something visually impressive but lacking its essential, appealing quality. Similarly, 'கற்றது உணர விரித்து உரையாதார்' refers to those who have acquired knowledge but cannot expand on it clearly for others to grasp. The comparison emphasizes that knowledge, like a flower's beauty, is unfulfilled if it cannot be effectively shared and appreciated by others.
